Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. input.content:
# Browser CAD Editor

A self-contained 2D CAD editor that runs entirely in the browser — no build step,
no dependencies. Just open `index.html`.

## Features

- **Tools**: select/move, line (chained), polyline, rectangle, circle, 3-point arc,
  linear dimension, text
- **Snapping**: adaptive grid snap plus object snap (endpoints, midpoints, centers,
  circle quadrants) with visual markers; Shift for ortho lock while drawing
- **Selection**: click, Shift+click to add, drag right for window select,
  drag left for crossing select; drag a selection to move it, Ctrl+drag to copy
- **Layers**: per-layer color and visibility, entities colored by layer or overridden
- **View**: wheel zoom at cursor, pan with middle/right drag or Space+drag, zoom-to-fit
- **Editing**: undo/redo (100 levels), properties panel (layer, color, circle radius,
  text content/size)
- **Files**: save/open JSON, export SVG, export DXF (R12 — opens in AutoCAD,
  LibreCAD, QCAD, etc.); the drawing also auto-persists to localStorage

## Keyboard shortcuts

| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| `S` `L` `P` `R` `C` `A` `D` `T` | select, line, polyline, rect, circle, arc, dimension, text |
| `Esc` | cancel current tool / deselect |
| `Enter` | finish polyline (`C` while drawing closes it) |
| `Shift` | ortho lock while drawing; add to selection when clicking |
| `Delete` | delete selection |
| `Ctrl+Z` / `Ctrl+Y` | undo / redo |
| `Ctrl+A` | select all |
| `Ctrl+S` | save JSON |
| `F` | zoom to fit |
| `G` / `O` | toggle grid snap / object snap |
| `?` | shortcut overlay |

## Coordinates

World coordinates are y-up (CAD convention) with the X axis drawn red and the
Y axis green. The grid adapts its spacing to the zoom level in 1-2-5 steps.

## Files

- `index.html` — page layout
- `style.css` — dark UI theme
- `app.js` — all editor logic (entities, tools, snapping, rendering, export)

Done. You have a working browser-based 2D CAD editor in `D:\physics\cad` — open `index.html` in any browser, no build step or dependencies. I verified it headlessly: drew all entity types via simulated mouse/keyboard with zero console errors, confirmed the rendering visually via screenshot, and validated that the SVG and DXF exporters produce well-formed output.

**What's in it:**

- **Drawing tools** — line (auto-chains like AutoCAD), polyline (Enter/double-click to finish, `C` to close), rectangle, circle, 3-point arc, linear dimensions (with extension lines, arrows, and live measurement text), and text. Shift gives ortho lock while drawing.
- **Snapping** — adaptive grid snap (1-2-5 spacing that follows zoom) plus object snap to endpoints, midpoints, centers, and circle quadrants, each with its own marker shape (square/triangle/circle). Toggle with `G`/`O` or the status-bar buttons.
- **Selection & editing** — click or Shift+click; drag right for window select, drag left for crossing select (AutoCAD-style). Drag a selection to move, Ctrl+drag to copy, Delete to remove, 100-level undo/redo.
- **Layers** — per-layer color and visibility, entities colored by-layer with per-entity override in the properties panel.
- **View** — wheel zoom at cursor, pan with middle/right drag or Space+drag, `F` to fit. World coordinates are y-up (CAD convention) with red X / green Y axes.
- **Files** — save/open JSON, export SVG, and export DXF R12 (opens in AutoCAD, LibreCAD, QCAD). The drawing also auto-saves to localStorage so refreshing doesn't lose work.

Press `?` in the app for the full shortcut list; `README.md` documents everything. The code is split as `index.html` (layout), `style.css` (dark theme), and `app.js` (~1,100 lines: entity model, snapping, tools, rendering, exporters) — so it's straightforward to extend with things like trim/fillet, more dimension types, or DXF import if you want to go further.
